text: Some watchers, however, were careless about their duty, and they would deliberately huddle together in a distant corner over a game of cards, plainly intending to allow him a little refreshment, which they imagined he kept hidden somewhere. <break time="0.8s" /> Nothing tormented him more than such watchers, and sometimes, overcoming his weakness, he sang for as long as he could during their watch, merely to show them how unjust their suspicion was. <break time="0.8s" /> Yet his singing did little good, since the watchers only marveled at the cleverness that allowed him, as they believed, to eat in secret even while he sang. <break time="0.8s" /> Far more welcome to him were the watchers who sat close to the bars and, not satisfied with the dim lighting of the hall, shone on him the electric torches supplied by the impresario. <break time="0.8s" /> The harsh light did not trouble him at all, since he could always doze a little anyway, and he gladly spent whole nights telling such watchers tales of his wandering life and listening to theirs in turn. <break time="0.8s" /> In the morning he was happiest, for then an enormous breakfast was brought to them at his own expense, and they fell upon it with the healthy appetite of men who had spent a long, sleepless night. <break time="0.8s" /> Since no one could watch him every minute of every day, no one but the artist himself could know whether his fast had truly been unbroken, and he alone, therefore, could be its fully satisfied spectator. <break time="0.8s" /> Yet he was never satisfied, and perhaps it was not fasting at all that had made him so terribly thin but his own dissatisfaction, for he alone knew what even the experts did not, namely how easy fasting was.
